module_title: Recent Amendments - NCBC, Anglo-Indians, and Boundaries
introduction: At this level, we look at the amendments dealing with specific demographic representations (Backward Classes and Anglo-Indians) and India's international land boundary adjustments.

core_concepts.title: 100th Amendment (2015) - Land Boundary Agreement
core_concepts.description: Gave effect to the acquiring of certain territories by India and the transfer of certain other territories to Bangladesh. This involved the exchange of 'enclaves' between the two countries to resolve border disputes.

core_concepts.title: 102nd Amendment (2018) - NCBC Status
core_concepts.description: Granted Constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC). Previously, it was only a statutory body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

core_concepts.title: 104th Amendment (2020) - SC/ST and Anglo-Indians
core_concepts.description: Extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies by another 10 years (up to 2030). Crucially, it did NOT extend the reservation for the Anglo-Indian community, effectively ending their nominated seats.

core_concepts.title: 105th Amendment (2021) - State OBC Lists
core_concepts.description: Restored the power of State governments to identify and maintain their own lists of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs/OBCs).

important_entities.name: Anglo-Indian Community
important_entities.significance: Previously, the President could nominate 2 Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha, and Governors could nominate 1 to State Assemblies. The 104th Amendment abolished this practice.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Don't confuse them. The 102nd created the constitutional NCBC. However, the Supreme Court interpreted it as taking away the States' power to list their own OBCs. The 105th was specifically passed to explicitly restore this power to the States.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Border (100) -> Tax (101) -> OBC (102) -> Poor General (103) -> SC/ST (104)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Memorize this flow: First we fixed borders, then taxes, then helped OBCs, then helped EWS, then extended SC/ST.

exam_strategy_tips: If a question asks which amendment ended Anglo-Indian nominations, the answer is the 104th Amendment.
The 100th Amendment modified the 1st Schedule of the Constitution to update the territorial boundaries of four states: Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya, and Tripura.
